children: UP signs 15 industry MoUs, issues five investor Letters of Comfort and partners with 13 academic institutions at the UP GCC Innovation Summit 2026 in Lucknow, as companies highlight investment opportunities in AI, product engineering and advanced technology

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has set a target of establishing 500 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in the state by 2031, positioning Uttar Pradesh as a destination for global business operations, advanced technology, product development and high-value employment.

At the UP GCC Innovation Summit 2026 in Lucknow on Monday, the state signed 15 memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with companies and talent partners, issued five Letters of Comfort (LoCs) to prospective investors, and exchanged MoUs with 13 academic institutions. The announcements are aimed at expanding investment, strengthening industry-academia collaboration and developing a workforce equipped for evolving global business requirements.

Organised by the IIT Kanpur Alumni Association in collaboration with Invest UP and HCLTech at Hotel The Centrum, the summit brought together business leaders, policymakers, investors and technology executives to discuss artificial intelligence (AI), digital transformation, product-led innovation and the future of global business services.

Yogi Adityanath said the state was ready to move beyond conventional business operations towards activities involving innovation, design, engineering and research. He cited its industrial base, skilled workforce, infrastructure and investor-focused policies as factors supporting its ambition to attract leading international companies.
Infrastructure And Talent Strengthen UP’s Investment Pitch

The Chief Minister highlighted developments in Uttar Pradesh’s investment environment since 2017, including single-window clearances and a focus on administrative efficiency. He said the state had strengthened investor confidence and moved beyond its earlier ‘BIMARU’ tag to become a revenue-surplus state.

Among the infrastructure and industrial advantages cited were an extensive expressway network, the country’s largest rail network, five international airports and an industrial land bank exceeding 75,000 acres. The state also accounts for 55% of India’s mobile manufacturing and 60% of its electronic components, according to the summit information.

Uttar Pradesh has an estimated 6.7 lakh professionals, including three lakh technology and engineering professionals. More than 8,000 higher education institutions and over two lakh STEM graduates annually provide a potential talent pipeline for companies looking to establish or expand operations.
Institutions including IIT Kanpur, IIT (BHU) Varanasi, IIM Lucknow, IIIT Lucknow and MNNIT Prayagraj contribute expertise in engineering, AI, analytics and management.

The state is also advancing initiatives such as its State AI Mission, deep-tech hubs, an AI City and a robotics cluster. These are intended to attract AI-led GCCs, product engineering teams, research and development facilities and advanced business services.
Five Investor Letters Of Comfort Issued

Five Letters of Comfort were issued to Havells India Limited, Ameriprise India LLP, MetLife Global Operations Support Centre Private Limited, LG Soft India Private Limited and WSP Consultants India Private Limited.
The LoC for WSP Consultants India Private Limited remains subject to approval by the Uttar Pradesh Industry Minister and issuance of the formal letter.

The letters form part of the state’s effort to convert investor interest into projects and strengthen its position in the GCC market. The announcements, however, represent investment facilitation steps rather than confirmation that every proposed project is already operational.
15 Industry MoUs Target GCC Growth And Skills

The 15 industry MoUs cover GCC expansion, technology-led investment and talent development. Companies named among the partners include EY GDS, AML RightSource, Computacenter, MetLife, DSV, DAMAC, Altruist and Smartworks.

Smartworks plans to establish two dedicated campuses in Lucknow. The state has also partnered with Paytm, AWS, Barclays, IBM and Naukri on training and skill-development programmes aligned with GCC requirements. Paytm signed two MoUs as part of the collaborations.

The partnerships are intended to support the growth of global business operations while helping employers access professionals with relevant technical and managerial skills. Their focus reflects the changing role of GCCs, which increasingly undertake specialised work beyond traditional support and delivery functions.
13 Academic Institutions Join Collaboration Drive

Uttar Pradesh exchanged MoUs with 13 academic institutions: IIT Kanpur, IIT Roorkee, IIM Lucknow, IIT (BHU) Varanasi, Aligarh Muslim University, Shiv Nadar University, MNNIT Allahabad, Lucknow University, IIIT Allahabad, IIIT Lucknow, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, Amity University and Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Technical University.

The partnerships aim to bring academic programmes closer to industry requirements and expand opportunities for practical training, research and industry-relevant skills development. Closer collaboration between universities and companies is expected to help students prepare for roles in AI, analytics, product engineering and global business services.
Seven Sessions Examine The Future Of GCCs

The summit featured seven thematic sessions on investment decisions, AI adoption, innovation and workforce development. Topics included the factors shaping GCC location choices, why companies may select Uttar Pradesh for future centres, and lessons from leaders building AI-first GCCs.

Other discussions examined the transition from service delivery to product ownership, GCC partnerships with start-ups and centres of excellence, the skills universities need to develop for the AI era, and workforce reskilling.
Industrial Development Minister Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’ also shared his views on the state’s GCC ecosystem, infrastructure and talent pool.
Companies Highlight Investment Experiences

Representatives of LG Electronics, Smartworks, Microsoft and HCL Technologies praised aspects of Uttar Pradesh’s policies, infrastructure and administrative support at the summit. The companies described projects and expansion plans that illustrate the range of technology activity taking place in the state.

LG Electronics representative Brijesh Sharma said the company was investing Rs 634 crore in its Eco Solutions GCC and aimed to begin operations by the end of 2026. The centre will focus on heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), heat pump technology and advanced product development, with more than 500 high-value jobs planned through talent development and training. The company also intends to expand research and development in AI-based data-centre cooling technologies.

Smartworks representative Harsh Binani said the company manages more than two million square feet of office space in Noida, occupied by over 110 companies, and is expanding into Lucknow. He said a 200,000-square-foot GCC hub had been developed at BBD Times Square.

Binani said the opportunity was to create career pathways for young people in cities including Lucknow, Kanpur and Gorakhpur. He emphasised that the focus should extend beyond signing MoUs to delivering projects and jobs.

Microsoft India Development Center representative Rajiv Kumar cited talent availability, employee safety, infrastructure and policy support as factors in the state’s investment appeal. He said that, when Microsoft was setting up its Noida centre, land was made available within about six weeks following discussions with Ritu Maheshwari, then chief executive of the Noida Authority.

According to Kumar, the centre employed around 600 people in its first year, growing to approximately 3,000 within three years. The campus was developed with an investment of around Rs 2,500 crore and has contributed to the development of technologies including Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Copilot.

HCL Technologies representative Kiran Cherukuri highlighted the state’s GCC policy and implementation of investment incentives. He said HCL had established its Lucknow campus around a decade ago and currently employed about 1,500 people there. He also cited an AI-powered GCC Centre of Excellence launched at the campus in collaboration with Amazon Web Services (AWS), intended to provide advanced cloud and computing facilities.
AI White Paper And Policy Incentives

During the summit, Yogi Adityanath released a white paper titled The True Economics of AI Adoption in GCCs, prepared under the deep-tech innovation collaboration between HCL and IIT Kanpur. The paper’s release placed AI adoption and its business implications among the event’s central themes.

The Uttar Pradesh GCC Policy 2024 offers eligible investors capital subsidies of up to 25% and land subsidies of up to 50%, alongside operational support, subject to the policy’s provisions and eligibility criteria. The incentives are intended to improve project viability and encourage companies to establish or expand high-value operations in the state.

The event was attended by Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’, Minister for Industrial Development, and Jaswant Singh Saini, Minister of State for Parliamentary Affairs and Industrial Development. Senior officials included Deepak Kumar, IIDC; Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary, Industry; Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary, IT and Electronics; Vijay Kiran Anand, chief executive of Invest UP; Invest UP ACEOs Prerna Sharma and Gazal Bharadwaj; and IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal.

Uttar Pradesh’s target of 500 GCCs by 2031 sets out an ambitious plan to expand its role in India’s knowledge economy. The next test will be translating investment commitments, institutional partnerships and policy incentives into operational centres, sustained hiring and opportunities for skilled professionals across the state.
